html:
The Wannsee Conference was a meeting of Nazi officials and state secretaries held on 20 January 1942 in a villa at Wannsee, a lake suburb of Berlin. It was called to coordinate the "Final Solution", the plan to murder the Jews of Europe.

Reinhard Heydrich, head of the SS security service, led it. Fifteen men attended, from the SS and from ministries of the state. Adolf Eichmann took the minutes. The record lists about eleven million Jews in Europe, in all countries including those not yet occupied, and lays out how they would be gathered and deported east.

The conference did not start the killing. Mass shootings in the east and the first gassings were already under way. Its purpose was to make sure every office of the state would cooperate under the SS. The one surviving copy of the minutes became key evidence after the war, and the villa is now a memorial. It matters for the story of the Holocaust because it shows that the murder was organised by ordinary officials as well as by fanatics.
